_note: AI constants. Every nation but the player's uses the same rules and the same default temperament; a scenario may override traits per nation (ai_traits) and give nations plans (ai_plans). Weights here are tuned in phase 6, step 8.

temperament._note: aggression and caution, 0 to 1. They scale the odds an AI wants before it attacks, the share of its army it commits and how readily it digs in or pulls back.

odds._note: Attacker power over defender power wanted before an advance: the bold (aggression 1, caution 0) ask for `bold`, the cautious (aggression 0, caution 1) for `cautious`.

value._note: AI.value of a province: its share of the owner's people and of its output (GDP plus industry), with a bonus when it is the capital.

threat._note: AI.threat: enemy power inside the province counts in full, power `hops` away is cut by `hop_decay` per hop; the sum is multiplied by 1 + stakes * value(province).

defense._note: reserve_share: share of a nation's power kept back as a reserve (scaled up by caution); needs reserve_min_armies armies. reserve_stay: the reserve moves only when another province is this many times more threatened than where it stands. merge_max_units: the most units in a stack the AI will form by merging. rebalance_ratio: an army changes front when one front is this many times better covered than another. retake_hops and retake_eta_spread: armies within that many hops, arriving within that many days of each other, may retake home ground. A front masses its armies on anchor provinces, one for every anchor_armies armies (at most anchor_max): the provinces with most threat plus anchor_value_weight times their value, chosen again every anchor_days. near_km: an unassigned army counts every near_km of distance to a front's anchors as one point of cover when choosing its front. rebalance_max_km: an army is moved to a worse-covered front only if it stands within this many km of it. plan_need: the need of a front facing an enemy the nation has an offensive plan against is multiplied by this (the main effort). settle_days: an army far from every line (over rebalance_max_km) is not sent to one until the nation's newest war is this many days old.

offense._note: max_share: share of a nation's power an aggression of 1 puts on offence. Target utility = w_plan * plan weight + w_value * AI.value + w_score * war score share + w_margin * (power over required odds, up to 2) - w_days * days to arrive - w_supply * supply hops; a target below min_utility is not attacked. retry_days: wait after finding nothing to attack. gather_days: give up if the force is not ready by then. fall_back_morale (scaled by 0.5 + caution) and fall_back_ratio (own power over the enemy's around the target): below them the stack falls back. plan_hops: how far an objective's weight reaches. reach_hops: armies this near may be sent, and reinforce_weight: the share of the power of enemy armies within support_hops that counts against an attack. odds_bold and odds_cautious: the odds wanted before a chosen battle (like `odds`, but for fighting only). max_campaigns: campaigns run at once, against different enemies. plan_odds_factor: an offensive plan against an enemy lowers the odds wanted against it to this share. gather_eta_share: only armies that can reach the staging province within this share of gather_days are picked. front_keep: an army may leave its front for an offence while the armies that stay keep this share of the power the front had.

forces._note: Recruiting. war_multiplier: war strength as a multiple of the peacetime army. per_turn: units started per turn. max_training: units in training at once. treasury_floor: the treasury is never taken below it, plus deficit_months of any deficit. income_share: units in training cost at most this share of horizon_months of revenue. train_hops: how far behind the most threatened line it raises. mix: share of each unit type in the force. demob_after_days: how long after its last war a nation at ease starts sending men home; demob_margin: the multiple of its peacetime army it keeps; demob_share: the share of the excess sent home each turn.

navy._note: AINavy and AILanding. Fleets of a nation at war are split by role in port (transports and submarines apart, and cruisers and destroyers detached as patrols) and then given a sea zone each: the cordon that would seal an enemy's ports from the open sea (a path-blocking search, narrowest zones first), the zones next to its own ports where enemy ships lie, and the zones where an escort is wanted for a landing. A zone's score = w_blockade / cordon size (or w_defend * its share of the nation's port trade, w_kill for a zone with enemy ships, w_escort) - w_days * days to get there; a fleet goes only where its power (with what is already sent there) is at least the nation's required odds times the enemy power in or around the zone (adjacent zones count adj_decay, fleets in port opening on it port_share). Below min_score it stays in, or goes to, port. A fleet whose nation is weaker (times sortie_ratio) than its enemies within theatre_hops zones of it seeks out neither the cordon nor the enemy's ships, only the waters by its ports; submarines go anyway. A zone already held by fleets sent there is worth stack_decay of its value to the next. repair_below / ready_strength: strength to go home and to sail again; range_factor: days at sea as a multiple of the shortest range before going home. replan_days: the pause between a fleet being given orders and a change of mind (it changes only for a gain of hysteresis). Landings: with no enemy ground across a land border, a nation with transports in port picks an enemy coast by AIOffense worth + w_margin * margin - w_days * days, needing power over the defenders times odds divided by the landing penalty; it gathers the armies (reach_hops by land) and the transports in the port, waits for its ships to hold the landing zone and the route (escort_days), then sends them. Building: at war, below build_ratio times the enemy fleets' power, one squadron at a time (max_building), by the type furthest below its share in the mix, if the treasury keeps build_floor, the hulls on the slips (this one too) draw at most income_share of the construction pool a day and the budget carries the upkeep (tolerance of net).

budget._note: AIBudget, once a month. Taxes: up by tax_step (to tax_max, or tax_max_war at war) when the nation is in debt and cannot repay it in repay_months, or runs a deficit its treasury cannot carry for cushion_months; down by tax_step to tax_min (under the default: light taxes help growth) when it is in surplus with more than rich_months of expenses in the bank, and then it also puts invest_share of its monthly surplus into state investment. Buildings: one a month, at most max_construction at a time, only when net is at least build_min_net; among the candidates richest provinces, the capital and ground behind the fronts, the one with the best yearly return per pound (min_return; food counts food_value, a railway near a front front_railway_bonus of the province's output, the capital times capital_multiplier), leaving build_floor in the treasury (double at war). Points: in a crisis, a batch is bought when the stock is under buy_below and buy_floor stays in the treasury.

diplomacy._note: AIDiplomacy. join: value = kind[kind] + w_ally_relation * opinion of the ally + w_enemy_relation * dislike of the enemies + w_border * share of enemies at its border + w_odds * (own side's share of power - 0.5) * 2 + w_support * war support above 50 - w_debt * debt (in months of revenue, at most 1) + w_decline * what declining costs; it joins at threshold. war: desire = w_hostile * dislike + w_grievance * grievance + w_plan if it has a plan against the target + w_cb if it has a casus belli; it never declares on a nation it made peace with in the last truce_days, nor without a motive of at least min_motive (desire without the casus belli); desire falls by neutral_penalty for a neutral target (Diplomacy.is_neutral) and by guaranteed_penalty for one a third power guarantees; it declares when desire * (0.5 + aggression) reaches declare_threshold and the odds (its side's power over the target's side, with allies and guarantors) reach its required odds times odds_margin. With no casus belli it also needs a plan, aggression of at least unjustified_min_aggression, odds of unjustified_odds, and room under the cap (unjustified_share_max in this file). treaties: once a month it may propose the treaty of greatest value at least propose_threshold (alliance: w_need * how much stronger a hostile neighbour is + w_bloc + w_relation; guarantee: w_menace * the menace to the guaranteed + w_bloc + w_relation; nap: w_need + w_relation; passage: w_passage when an enemy lies beyond a neutral) and improve relations with a friend (within improve_window of the alliance bar) or a strong neighbour (improve_threshold), always keeping points_reserve diplomacy points. rival_relation: a neighbour below it is a rival.

peace._note: AIPeace. urge = -score * k_score + k_support * (support_ref - war support, if positive) + k_debt * months of revenue owed (at most debt_cap_months) + k_days_per_month * months at war + k_quiet * months without a battle beyond quiet_grace_months + capital_lost if the enemy holds the capital - k_ally * allies still fighting (less by ally_boldness_discount for the bold). A nation made to give accepts terms costing no more than its urge, if its score is at most -loss_floor or its urge is at least seek_threshold; a white peace is taken while urge is at least -white_tolerance; offered terms are taken if they cost at least accept_share of the taker's score. Past seek_threshold a nation proposes peace; with score at least demand_score and war aims met by aims_enough it names its price: up to demand_budget_share of its score in provinces (aims first), then an indemnity of at most indemnity_max_share over indemnity_months. afford_share: the most of its monthly revenue a nation will commit to indemnities.

variety._note: What the game's seed (GameState.ai_seed, chosen when a new game starts) varies. temperament: each nation's aggression and caution move by up to this much. target: the utility of each target an offence weighs moves by up to this much (fresh every month). Seed 0 varies nothing.

ambition._note: Ambitions begin only start_delay_days after the scenario starts, so the opening crisis plays out as scripted. AIAmbition: what an AI nation wants once the opening crisis is over. Every review_days a nation at peace with an aggression of at least min_aggression looks over its land neighbours it could declare on (not allied, no truce) where its side has odds_margin times the odds it needs, and scores each: w_claim if it holds a casus belli, plus w_hostile * how little the target likes it, w_grievance * its grievance, w_weak * how much smaller the target's economy is, plus w_opportunity * how far the odds are past what it needs (a tenfold margin counts in full), less w_guarantee for each guarantor of the target, less w_neutral for a nation that stands apart (Diplomacy.is_neutral). The best above threshold becomes its ambition: a plan (objectives on the target's border provinces and its capital) is made, the nation mobilizes to `mobilization`, works for a casus belli if it has none (AIDiplomacy.consider_justify) and declares when the ordinary rules allow. An ambition is dropped if the target stops being a fit, after give_up_days, or when the nation goes to war; cooldown_days must pass before the next. Peacetime rebuilding: a nation under rebuild_share of its peacetime army raises units at its capital.

munitions._note: AIBudget's arms share (see scripts/sim/munitions.gd): peace_share plus peace_per_tension times tension (0..1) in calm years, crisis_share when mobilized, in a crisis or with a case built against it, war_share at war. At war it buys munitions abroad when its stockpile would last fewer than min_days of all-out war, spending at most buy_treasury_share of its treasury a month.

coalition._note: Nations on one side of a war act as a coalition (scripts/ai/ai_coalition.gd). claim_penalty: utility an offence loses when an ally already aims a campaign at the same province, so allies do not crowd one front. hold (off in Historical, on in the Challenging difficulty): an AI nation does not make a separate peace while allies fight on, unless it is strained (war support at or below strain_support, its capital lost, or a war score at or below minus strain_score). partner_urge: the share of seek_threshold an ally's wish for peace must reach for it to join a joint peace (a conference) the nation proposes.
